in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

SPECIFICATION  FOR 
FLAT  FORM  SPRINGS 

PARTI  DESIGN  AND  CALCULATION  FOT^  SPRINGS  MADE 
FROM  RECTANGULAR  COLD-ROLLED  STRIPS 


1.  Scope — Lays  down  calculations  for  design  of  flat  formed  springs  made  from  rectangular  cold- 
rolled  strips. 

1.1  It  applies  to  cold-formed  springs  with  material  thickness  up  to  3'0  mm. 

1 .2  It  does  not  cover  the  design  and  calculations  of  disc  springs  and  similar  products. 

2.  Terminology  —  Following  symbols  and  units  shall  apply  (  see  Fig.  1  ). 

b        =  Width  of  spring  mm 

5         =  Thickness  of  spring  mm 

E        =  Modulus  of  elasticity  N/mm^ 

/         =  Deflection  of  spring  mm 

/i...    ^n       =  Deflection  of  spring  associated  with  spring  foroes  Fi...Fn  mm 

h        =  Stroke,  difference  between  two  load  lengths  mm 

/7o       ==  Unloaded  height  of  spring  mm 

/?!...  hn      =  Heights  of  loaded  spring  corresponding  to  the  spring  forces  Fi...Fn  mm 

k        =  Coefficient  ( bending  stress  correction  factor ) 

/         =  Effective  length  of  spring  mm 

D*      =  Total  developed/blank  dimension  mm 

F        =  Spring  force  N 

Ft...  Fn       ==  Spring  forces  corresponding  to  spring  deflections  /7i...hn  N 

R        =  Radius  assumed  by  the  spring  on  loading  mm 

r  m\n    =  Minimum  radius  {see  Fig.  6  )  mm 

=  Ultimate  tensile  strength  of  the  strip  N/mm^ 

»  Uncorrected  bending  stress  N/mm^ 

=  Corrected  bending  stress  N/mm^ 

t^bi.-  <Jbn      =  Uncorrected  bendmg  stress  corresponding  to  spring  forces  Fx...Fn  N/mm^ 

cbik...<'bnk    ^  Corrected  bending  stress  corresponding  to  spring  forces  Fx,.,Fn  N/mm^ 

a^^      =  Uncorrected  strokestress  i.e.,  the  difference  between  bending  stresses  at  hi  and  h2  N/mm^ 

(^bnk      =  Corrected  stroke  stress  i.e.,  the  difference  between  bending  stresses  at  hi  and  h^  N/mm^ 

=  Permissible  stroke  stress  N/mm^

3.  Modes  of  Loading  —  Before  any  calculations  are  made  it  should,  as  a  rule,  be  established  whether 
under  the  type  of  loading  envisaged  the  springs  will  be  subjected  to  static  or  infrequently  varying  load 
or  to  alternating  or  dynamic  loading. 

3.1  Static  or  Infrequently  Varying  Load —  Springs  under  static  load  or  infrequently  varying  load  are  : 

a)  all  springs  which  carry  only  static  loads;  and 

b)  all   springs  to  which  occasional  load  variations  are  applied  at  fairly  long  intervals  and  at  less 
than  10  000  load  cycles  during  life  envisaged. 

Z,2  Alternating  Load — Flat  springs  subjected  to  alternating  load  are  springs  that  have  applied  to 
them  a  load  which  alternates  over  the  height  range  '/?'  between  spring  loads  fi  and  F^, 


'  Total  developed/blank  dimension  =-  approx  dimension  of  strip  required  to  form  the  spring.

Note  1  —  For  formulae  (1)  and  (6),  designer  can  calculate  the  proportion  *b'  and  V  for  given  value  of  force  'F' 
deflection  Y'  spring  length  7'  and  Young's  modulus  '£'. 

Not^^  2  —  The  beam  formulae  (1)  to  (6)  are  valid  only  if  the  maximum  deflection  T  is  not  exceeding  25  percent  of 
the  length  of  the  spring. 

Note  3  —  Formulae  (1)  to  (6)  have  to  be  modified  In  those  cases  where  the  spring  is  built  up  of  several  leaves.

6.  Modulus  of  elasticity  for  strips  for  design  of  flat  formed  springs  is  as  given  below: 

S/  No,  Material  Modulus  of  Elasticity 

i)  Cold  rolled  steel  strip  for  springs  as  per  206  000  N/mm^ 

IS  :  2507-1975  'Cold-rolled  steel  strip 
for  spring  ( first  revision)' 

ii)  Austentic  stainless  steel   strip  as  per  190  200  N/mm^ 

IS  :  6011  "  1972   'Stainless  steel  plate 
sheet  and  strip' 

ill)  Phosphor     bronze      strips       as      per  105  000  N/mm^ 

IS:  7814-1975  'Phosphor  bronze  sheet 
strip  and  foil' 

iv)  Copper  beryllium  strips  127  000  N/mm^ 

6.1  The  modulus  of  elasticity  values  specified  at  SI  No.  (ii),  (iii)  and  (iv)  above  are  for  general  guidance 
only.     Reference  may  be  made  to  the  material  manufacturer  for  more  exact  values.

10.  Finish  —  As  specified  in  IS  :  10878  (  Part  2  )-1984  'Flat  form  springs  :  Part   2  Specification  for 
springs  made  from  rectangular  cold-rolled  strips'. 

EXPLANATORY     NOTE 

This  standard   is   Part   1  of  Indian  Standard  on  the  design  calculation   and  specification  of  flat 
form  springs.    This  part  deals  with  design  and  calculations,  while  Part  2  covers  the  specification.
